# Cover Letter

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Community Engagement Officer position with your library service. Having grown up in Exeter and worked in community-facing roles here for the past five years, I am genuinely committed to widening access to public services and would relish the opportunity to help your libraries become even more welcoming and central to the communities they serve.

My most directly relevant experience comes from my three years as Volunteer Coordinator at a local food bank, where I recruit, induct and support around sixty volunteers across four distribution centres. This has given me substantial expertise in volunteer management at scale, including developing safeguarding training and implementing retention strategies. I am confident I can successfully manage and develop your team of forty volunteers, ensuring they feel valued and equipped to deliver excellent community experiences.

Throughout my two years as Events Assistant at an independent theatre in Exeter, I gained hands-on experience planning and delivering public programmes. I co-ran a schools outreach initiative and coordinated monthly community open days, both of which honed my ability to design activities for diverse audiences and build lasting partnerships with schools and local organisations. Several of the schools and community groups I worked with then remain contacts of mine, which will be valuable in building the partnerships essential to your role.

I have demonstrated capability in financial management and reporting. I oversee a £12,000 annual budget for volunteer expenses and training, and produce monthly reports to our trustees covering participation metrics, volunteer retention and impact. Last year, I contributed significantly to a successful £25,000 grant application, compiling participation data and case studies that evidenced our community need and impact. Whilst the budget I would manage in this role is considerably larger, my experience demonstrates that I understand the importance of rigorous financial planning, value for money and clear accountability.

What drew me to this role is its genuine focus on reducing barriers to access. My food bank work has reinforced my conviction that public services must actively reach those not currently engaged, rather than waiting passively for communities to come to them. I am enthusiastic about designing programmes that speak to people across Exeter—from young children through to older residents—and measuring whether we are truly serving everyone.

I am eager to bring my community engagement experience and local knowledge to your library service. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your vision.

Yours faithfully,

[Your Name]
